result_text:
Any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` now counts as a mock-resources folder, so files under it are classified as test code. The scoping and convention tests I ran pass. I did not add new tests or try the new cases by hand.

I changed the two "Mock resources" regexes in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java` (around line 393). They now read `.*/__mock[^/]*/.*` and `.*/mock[^/]*/.*`. Before, they required one or more characters from `[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]` after `mock`.

What that gives you, going by how the patterns match rather than by running them:
- **Newly caught:** plain `mock/`, `mock.data/`, `mock(old)/`, `mock-größe/` and `mock模拟/`.
- **Still caught:** `mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/` and `mockStore/`.
- **Not caught:** `remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, and files named `mock.java` or `mockery.java`. The match needs a `/` right before `mock` and stops at the next `/`, so it stays inside one folder name.
- **Backslash paths:** `SourceFileFilter.matches` already tries each path with `\` converted to `/`, so no extra handling was needed.

I did not run the full test suite.
